title: Microsoft Purview: permanently delete OneDrive and SharePoint files with Priority cleanup
summary: The control paths, audit search, rollout dates and admin opt-in behavior are supported. The page passes with one minor citation gap: its description of Information Protection and Governance as an add-on needs the supporting Microsoft reference.

claims.claim: Purview Data Lifecycle Management adds a Delete data permanently option to Priority cleanup for SharePoint and OneDrive files.
claims.quote: Permanent deletion is an additional option for a Priority Cleanup policy.

claims.claim: Permanent deletion bypasses the SharePoint and OneDrive recycle bins, removing that recovery stage.
claims.quote: This option bypasses the SharePoint and OneDrive recycle bins.

claims.quote: Permanent deletion can override retention settings or eDiscovery holds.

claims.claim: A licensing rule specific to the permanent-deletion option is not yet published, distinct from the documented Priority cleanup entitlement.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" licensing price meter; read the permanent-deletion prerequisites and the Purview service description's Priority cleanup licensing passage; neither specifies a separate entitlement for this option.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a price specific to the permanent-deletion option as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" licensing price meter; opened the permanent-deletion page and Purview service description, including its Data Lifecycle & Records Management licensing section; no option-specific price was stated.

claims.claim: No meter or per-deletion charge is documented for this option as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" licensing price meter; read the permanent-deletion page and the service description's Data Lifecycle & Records Management section; no permanent-deletion meter or per-deletion rate was documented.

claims.claim: The permanent-deletion page lists roles, approvers, auditing and simulation prerequisites without naming a license.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" licensing price meter; read the complete permanent-deletion page, including Prerequisites and its link to the service description; its prerequisites name no license.

claims.claim: The policy-creation path reaches Delete data permanently through the documented Static and Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive choices.
claims.quote:
go to Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup.
2. Select + Create a priority cleanup.
3. Enter the policy name and description, choose an adaptive or static scope
4. On the Choose what to do with the content page, select Delete data permanently.

claims.claim: The general workflow supplies the intermediate labels Choose the type of priority cleanup > Static > Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive.
claims.quote:
For Choose the type of priority cleanup, select Adaptive or Static then select Next.
For Static scope, select Policy for SharePoint/OneDrive

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a PowerShell or API call that creates a policy with the permanent-deletion option.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" PowerShell New-ComplianceTag API; read the permanent-deletion workflow and New-ComplianceTag, Set-RetentionCompliancePolicy and New-RetentionComplianceRule references; no call selects this option.

claims.claim: The Priority Cleanup Admin role is required to create and manage these policies.
claims.quote: Assign the Priority Cleanup Admin role to the administrator who creates and manages the policy.

claims.claim: The Security & Compliance PowerShell New-ComplianceTag reference lists a PriorityCleanup parameter set and switch.
claims.quote:
### PriorityCleanup
New-ComplianceTag
    [-Name] <String>
    -RetentionAction <String>
    -RetentionDuration <Unlimited>
    -RetentionType <String>
    -MultiStageReviewProperty <String>
    [-PriorityCleanup]

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The tenant switch is in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management.
From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings.
From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a PowerShell or API operation for the tenant Priority cleanup switch as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "turn off" PowerShell tenant configuration; read Turn off priority cleanup for the tenant and the retention policy PowerShell reference; results document the portal switch, not a tenant-switch command or API.

claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for Exchange as well as for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Approvers use Microsoft Purview portal > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups > cleanup > Approve disposal.
claims.quote:
go to Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups.
2. Select the cleanup and review the identified items, their locations, and their history.
3. Select the items to delete, and then select Approve disposal.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a PowerShell or API call for approving Priority cleanup items as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "approve" "PowerShell" API; "priority cleanup" "approve disposal" API Microsoft Graph PowerShell -Exchange -mailboxes. Read permanent-deletion approval steps and Set-ComplianceTag reference excerpts; no item-approval call was documented.

claims.claim: An approver sees only the items assigned to that person in Pending cleanups.
claims.quote: each person that accesses the Priority cleanup > Pending cleanups page sees only items that they're assigned to approve.

claims.quote:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog can search a date range with -Operations PriorityCleanupFileDeleted and -FreeText containing the cleanup ID.
claims.quote:
The FreeText parameter filters the log entries by the specified text string.
The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.where: controls[3].note; controls[3].api; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Searching with the cleanup ID and checking PriorityCleanupFileDeleted monitors permanent deletion.
claims.quote:
In the auditing solution, use the cleanup ID as the keyword search string.
4. Check for the PriorityCleanupFileDeleted operation, which indicates that Priority Cleanup permanently deleted an item.

claims.claim: The roadmap description says retention policies and labels keep deleted SharePoint and OneDrive content in recycle bins for 93 days.
claims.quote: M365 retention labels policies and M365 retention policies do not hard delete content immediately and keeps the data in Recycle Bins for 93 days for ODSP.

claims.claim: Microsoft positions the option as reducing exposure from growing Copilot-related content, including Teams transcripts.
claims.quote:
This capability helps reduce data exposure risk from rapidly growing Copilot-related content
Review your organization's data risk and retention strategy, especially for Copilot-generated content such as Teams transcripts.

claims.claim: The roadmap identifies managing data spillage as a use case.
claims.quote: Priority Cleanup feature allows users to bypass retention, and eDiscovery holds to help customers comply to changing legal/compliance requirements or manage data spillage scenarios.

claims.claim: The general tenant-level Priority cleanup control is enabled by default, distinct from configuring permanent deletion.
claims.quote: Because of the built-in safeguards, the feature itself is enabled by default at the tenant level.

claims.claim: The overview says review-set data is automatically deleted when an eDiscovery admin deletes the entire case.
claims.quote: This data is automatically deleted when the entire eDiscovery case is deleted by an eDiscovery admin.

claims.claim: Learn's overview describes overriding Preservation Lock for delete-only settings.
claims.quote: Because the deletion from priority cleanup can override existing holds and even Preservation Lock when the retention settings are for delete-only, the process requires multiple approvals, specific roles, and is audited.

claims.claim: The same Learn page's Limitations section says delete-only Preservation Lock items are not in scope outside simulation, and the briefing reports that conflict.
claims.quote: In simulation mode, items under preservation lock where the retention settings are configured for delete-only may show up. These items are not actually in scope for priority cleanup outside simulation mode.

claims.claim: Priority Cleanup Admin is automatically added to the Organization Management role group.
claims.quote: This role is automatically added to the Organization Management role group but must be manually added to any other role group.

claims.claim: Each item requires deletion approval from at least one person other than the policy creator.
claims.quote: each item subject to priority cleanup always requires at least one other person to approve the deletion in addition to the person who created the priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: Items subject to eDiscovery holds require eDiscovery admin approval.
claims.quote: If an item is also subject to one or more eDiscovery holds, eDiscovery admin approval is also required.

claims.claim: Learn recommends leaving the policy running for continually created Teams recordings and transcripts.
claims.quote: Because these files are continually created, leave the priority cleanup policy running to automatically find and delete the stale files.

claims.claim: Policy creation fails if the eDiscovery reviewer lacks the correct roles in advance.
claims.quote: If the reviewer for eDiscovery admin doesn't have the correct roles assigned in advance, policy creation fails with an error.

claims.claim: One Priority cleanup policy cannot cover Exchange, SharePoint and OneDrive together.
claims.quote: you can't create a cleanup policy for all three locations in same policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a separate tenant switch for permanent deletion alone as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "permanent deletion" "switch" disable; read the permanent-deletion configuration and the SharePoint/OneDrive tenant-switch instructions; these document explicit policy selection and the general switch, not a separate tenant switch.
